title: Msemen
subtitle: Moroccan layered flatbread
excerpt: Msemen are square Moroccan flatbreads with a layered, flaky interior and a crisp golden exterior. Folded with oil and semolina before cooking, they tear into thin sheets. Makes 8 pieces, serves 4.
sourceNotes: A staple of Moroccan breakfast and tea time, eaten with honey, amlou (argan nut butter) or alongside harira. Msemen is also made savoury with a kefta meat filling.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze cooked msemen between sheets of parchment for up to 2 months. Reheat in a dry pan.
recipe.batchNotes: Make a double batch. They reheat well and keep in the fridge for 3 days.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Dough can rest in the fridge overnight after the initial 30-minute rest.
recipe.temperatureNote: Cook in a dry pan over medium heat. No oil in the pan.

glossaryTerms.definition: The process of folding oil and semolina into flatbread dough to create separated layers. The dough is stretched, oiled, folded and then pan-fried so the layers puff and crisp.
Leaving the dough after kneading allows the gluten to relax. Relaxed dough stretches without springing back, making it possible to roll the msemen thin enough for good layers.

for 30 minutes after kneading makes this possible.
Oil your hands and work surface rather than flouring them. Oil keeps the dough extensible; flour stiffens it and stops the layers forming properly.

items.prepNote: fine semolina, divided: 50g in dough, 50g for laminating

content.text: Mix plain flour, 50g semolina and salt in a bowl. Gradually add 180ml warm water, mixing until a soft dough forms. Knead for 8 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Divide the dough into 8 balls. Oil the balls lightly and cover with a damp cloth. Rest for 30 minutes.
Oil your hands and work surface. Take one dough ball and flatten with your palm. Stretch gently with your fingers until paper-thin.
Brush the surface with oil. Scatter over a pinch of fine semolina. Fold the dough into thirds like a letter. Fold again to make a square. The finished square should be around 10cm.
Repeat with all balls. Rest the squares for 5 minutes.
Heat a dry pan over medium heat. Flatten each square with your palm or a rolling pin to about 15cm. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden with brown patches.
Serve warm with honey, butter or alongside harira soup.

attrs.symptom: Dough springs back and tears when stretching
attrs.fix: Cover and rest for a further 10 minutes. The dough should stretch to translucent without tearing.

attrs.cause: Not enough oil or semolina between layers, or not folded thin enough
attrs.fix: The stretch step is critical. The dough must be nearly see-through before folding. Use a generous brush of oil each time.

content.text: Msemen is eaten across Morocco at breakfast and at the afternoon tea meal called ftour. In cities like Marrakech and Casablanca, msemen sellers set up griddles from early morning, cooking to order and stacking the squares in cloth-covered piles. The same technique is used to make meloui (round spiralled flatbreads) by rolling the laminated dough into a log before cooking. A Tunisian equivalent called mlawi is made the same way.
